summary: Seeded the .seventwos upstream policy/state/path-map/invariants system for usr-workspace-android.

Diagnosed root cause of startup_failure on all push-triggered workflow runs against develop (Test, APK Build, Code Quality Checks): the repository's GitHub Actions allowed-actions policy is set to 'selected' with patterns_allowed [astral-sh/*, dorny/*, Azure/*, azure/*, codecov/*, dependabot/*] and verified_allowed=false. tests.yml/build.yml/quality.yml use third-party actions not covered by this list (jlumbroso/free-disk-space, nschloe/action-cached-lfs-checkout, webfactory/ssh-agent, gradle/actions/setup-gradle), so GitHub refuses to start those jobs. The Graphify workflow is unaffected because it only uses actions already covered by the allow-list, which is why it ran to completion (and failed at runtime, not startup) while the others failed at startup with 0s duration.
evidence: gh run list --limit 15 (all push@develop runs conclusion=startup_failure, 0s duration)

summary: Attempted to repair the PR validation baseline by expanding the repo-level actions/permissions/selected-actions allow-list to cover the actions already pinned-by-SHA in existing workflows (actions-ecosystem, gradle-update, gradle, jlumbroso, ludeeus, nschloe, peaceiris, peter-evans, reactivecircus, webfactory, zizmorcore). The API call was rejected with HTTP 409: 'Selected actions and workflows are already set at the organization or enterprise level.' This confirms the allow-list is enforced above the repository and cannot be repaired from within this repository; it requires an org/enterprise administrator. Recorded as a blocker rather than worked around by disabling or rewriting the affected checks.

Follow-up hardening of the .seventwos validator per review findings: added hardcoded expected fork/upstream identity constants and full-SHA-format checks; opt-in --verify-git-identity commit-object-existence and merge-base recomputation against state.yml's seed; fail-closed git-show ref resolution (distinguishing unresolvable-ref / conclusively-absent-path / other-error) used consistently for ledger append-only checks, a new state.yml seed byte-immutability check, and new anti-weakening protection for invariants.yml/policy.yml/path-map.yml requiring a machine-verifiable ledger.jsonl justification (change_type/target_ids/rationale) for any removal or field change to an existing entry, still human-gated via normal PR review; exact per-event-type base SHA usage (pull_request.base.sha / push before / merge_group.base_sha) in the policy-validate workflow instead of a moving branch ref; assessment-artifact immutability extended to reject rename/copy/type-change and require new files be regular files (not symlinks); the policy-validate workflow now also triggers on changes to the sibling upstream-assessment workflow and structurally validates both workflows for read-only permissions, full-SHA-pinned actions, persist-credentials:false, no submodule checkout, and no secrets references; and extended compatibility_sensitive_identifier coverage to Java source roots and Gradle build files/content.
rationale: Extended the compatibility_sensitive_identifier category's description and paths to explicitly cover Java source roots and Gradle build files/content-level io.element identifiers (review finding #6): this is an additive coverage expansion, not a weakening, but the description text itself changed so it requires this justification entry under the same anti-weakening protection that applies to any semantic edit.
